Practical Framework

Prompt Optimisation: Better Outputs, Lower Cost, Faster Shipping

A deliberate approach to prompt engineering that turns every token into measurable value

The Problem

Ad-hoc prompting silently drains budget, quality, and velocity

Three compounding costs most teams overlook

  • Inconsistent outputs — Without structured prompts, the same query yields wildly different results, forcing manual review and rework every time
  • Wasted tokens & inflated cost — Naive prompts consume 30–50% more tokens than structured alternatives, a gap that scales with every API call
  • Slow iteration cycles — Teams typically need 3–5 revision rounds to reach production-grade quality, burning engineering hours on trial and error
Every unoptimised prompt is a recurring tax — on spend, on consistency, and on time-to-value. These costs compound with every new use case you ship.
Source: Industry benchmarks (OpenAI, Anthropic best-practice guides)1

Prompt Design Patterns

Four composable patterns cover the vast majority of prompt optimisation needs

A mental model for systematic prompt engineering

  • System-prompt framing — Set the model's role, constraints, and tone up front to anchor every response
  • Few-shot examples — Supply 2–5 input/output pairs so the model learns your format by demonstration
  • Chain-of-thought reasoning — Ask the model to "think step by step" to improve accuracy on complex tasks
  • Structured output formatting — Request JSON, Markdown, or tables to cut post-processing and reduce token waste by 30–50%
When to combine: Pair few-shot examples with chain-of-thought for up to 40% better output consistency — start simple, then layer patterns as needed across 3–5 iteration cycles.

Action Plan

Adopt this five-step checklist for every new LLM feature

A repeatable process your team can start using this sprint

  • Define task scope — Specify the input, desired output format, and constraints before writing a single token
  • Choose prompt patterns — Select from few-shot, chain-of-thought, or structured templates based on task complexity
  • Write eval criteria — Set measurable quality bars (accuracy, consistency, token efficiency) before iterating
  • Run your test suite — Validate against edge cases across 3–5 iteration cycles to reach production-grade quality
  • Document the winning prompt — Record the final prompt, rationale, and eval results so the team can reuse and improve it
Start this sprint: Apply this checklist to your next LLM feature — no new tooling required. Structured prompts cut token waste by 30–50% and boost output consistency by up to 40%.
